findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant isolation for document reads
findings.body: When `userTenant` differs from `documentTenant`, this function now still returns `true`. Any caller relying on this authorization predicate can expose documents across tenant boundaries; retain the equality check or an equivalent authorization decision.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported document label contract
findings.body: The exact value of exported `documentLabel` changes from `"Document"` to `"Document record"`, also changing its inferred TypeScript literal type. Under the stated requirement to preserve contracts, exact-value integrations and type-level consumers can break; retain the exported value or introduce a separate display label.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant equality enforcement
findings.body:
`canReadDocument` now authorizes every request. Any user whose `userTenant` differs from a document’s `documentTenant` can read that cross-tenant document, creating an authorization bypass and data exposure.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported document label contract
findings.body:
The exported value and its inferred TypeScript literal type changed from `"Document"` to `"Document record"`. Downstream consumers typed against `"Document"` will no longer compile, while integrations or tests matching the established exact value will fail.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant isolation in `canReadDocument`
findings.body:
Returning `true` unconditionally authorizes document reads when `userTenant !== documentTenant`, enabling any caller relying on this exported authorization check to expose documents across tenant boundaries.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
